title: MATH GAOKAO - 383
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Locus of a Circle in the Complex Plane
questions.learningObjective: Identify the geometric locus defined by an equation of the form \(|z-z_0|=r\).
questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) in the complex plane satisfying \(|z-(2+3i)|=5\) is

options.label: A
options.text: a circle centered at \(2+3i\) with radius \(5\).

options.label: B
options.text: a circle centered at \(-2-3i\) with radius \(5\).

questions.explanation: The equation \(|z-z_0|=r\) describes the set of points whose distance from \(z_0\) is \(r\). Here \(z_0=2+3i\) and \(r=5\), so the locus is a circle centered at \(2+3i\) with radius \(5\).
questions.hint: Recall that \(|z-z_0|\) represents the distance from \(z\) to the point \(z_0\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the locus of points equidistant from two given complex points.
questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-3|=|z+2i|\) is

options.label: A
options.text: the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining \(3\) and \(-2i\).

options.label: B
options.text: the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining \(3\) and \(2i\).

questions.explanation: The quantities \(|z-3|\) and \(|z+2i|=|z-(-2i)|\) are distances from \(z\) to \(3\) and \(-2i\), respectively. Points equidistant from these two distinct fixed points lie on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. The distractor uses the wrong sign for the second fixed point.
questions.hint: Rewrite each modulus in the form of a distance to a fixed complex number.

questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(\arg(z-1)=\frac{\pi}{4}\) is

options.label: A
options.text: the full line through \(1\) with slope \(1\).

options.label: B
options.text: the ray starting at \(1\), making an angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) with the positive real axis, and not including \(1\).

questions.explanation: Let \(w=z-1\). The condition \(\arg(w)=\frac{\pi}{4}\) means \(w\ne 0\) and \(w\) lies on the ray from the origin at angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\). Translating by \(1\), the locus is the ray starting at \(1\) in direction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\), excluding the starting point \(1\).
questions.hint: Consider the direction of the complex number \(z-1\) after translating the origin to \(1\).

questions.concept: Ellipse as a Sum of Distances
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the locus defined by a constant sum of distances to two fixed points.
questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-1|+|z+1|=4\) is

options.label: A
options.text: an ellipse with foci at \(1\) and \(-1\) and major axis length \(2\).

options.label: B
options.text: an ellipse with foci at \(1\) and \(-1\) and major axis length \(4\).

questions.explanation: The equation \(|z-1|+|z+1|=4\) says that the sum of distances from \(z\) to \(1\) and \(-1\) is \(4\). For an ellipse, this constant sum equals the major axis length \(2a\). Hence \(2a=4\), so the major axis length is \(4\), with foci at \(1\) and \(-1\).
questions.hint: Compare the given equation with the standard focal property of an ellipse.

questions.concept: Disk Defined by a Modulus Inequality
questions.learningObjective: Interpret \(|z-z_0|\le r\) as a closed disk in the complex plane.
questions.question: The set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-2i|\le 3\) is

options.label: A
options.text: the circle centered at \(2i\) with radius \(3\).

options.label: B
options.text: the closed disk centered at \(2i\) with radius \(3\).

questions.explanation: The inequality \(|z-2i|\le 3\) means that the distance from \(z\) to \(2i\) is at most \(3\). Therefore the locus is the closed disk centered at \(2i\) with radius \(3\), including its boundary circle.
questions.hint: Decide whether the inequality describes only the boundary or all points within a fixed distance.

questions.concept: Apollonius Circle from a Distance Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Find the circle determined by a constant ratio of distances to two fixed points.
questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-1|=2|z-2|\) is

options.label: A
options.text: a circle centered at \(\frac{7}{3}\) with radius \(\frac{2}{3}\).

options.label: B
options.text: a circle centered at \(\frac{7}{3}\) with radius \(\frac{4}{3}\).

questions.explanation:
Let \(z=x+iy\). Squaring gives
\[
(x-1)^2+y^2=4\bigl((x-2)^2+y^2\bigr).
\]
Expanding and simplifying:
\[
3x^2-14x+3y^2+15=0,
\]
so
\[
\left(x-\frac{7}{3}\right)^2+y^2=\frac{4}{9}.
\]
Thus the locus is a circle centered at \(\frac{7}{3}\) with radius \(\frac{2}{3}\).
questions.hint: Square both sides and write \(z=x+iy\) to convert the modulus equation into an equation in \(x\) and \(y\).

questions.concept: Argument of a Translated Complex Number
questions.learningObjective: Identify a ray from an argument equation involving a translated point.
questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(\arg(z+2i)=\frac{3\pi}{4}\) is

options.label: A
options.text: the ray starting at \((0,2)\) at angle \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\), excluding \((0,2)\).

options.label: B
options.text: the ray starting at \((0,-2)\) at angle \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\), excluding \((0,-2)\).

questions.explanation: Since \(z+2i=z-(-2i)\), the condition is \(\arg(z-(-2i))=\frac{3\pi}{4}\). The point \(-2i\) corresponds to \((0,-2)\). Therefore the locus is the ray starting at \((0,-2)\) at angle \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\), excluding the starting point.
questions.hint: Rewrite \(z+2i\) as \(z-(-2i)\) to identify the translated origin.

questions.concept: Half-Plane from an Inequality of Distances
questions.question: The set of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-1|\le |z+1|\) is

options.label: A
options.text: \(\{z:\operatorname{Re}(z)\ge 0\}\).

options.label: B
options.text: \(\{z:\operatorname{Re}(z)\le 0\}\).

questions.explanation:
Let \(z=x+iy\). Squaring the inequality gives
\[
(x-1)^2+y^2\le (x+1)^2+y^2.
\]
Simplifying,
\[
x^2-2x+1\le x^2+2x+1,
\]
so \(-2x\le 2x\), which gives \(x\ge 0\). Thus the region is \(\operatorname{Re}(z)\ge 0\).
questions.hint: Square both sides and compare the resulting expressions in terms of \(x=\operatorname{Re}(z)\).

questions.concept: Circle from a Sum of Squared Distances
questions.learningObjective: Convert an equation involving squared moduli into a circle equation.
questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(|z-1|^2+|z+1|^2=6\) is

options.label: A
options.text: a circle centered at the origin with radius \(\sqrt{2}\).

options.label: B
options.text: a circle centered at the origin with radius \(2\).

questions.explanation:
Let \(z=x+iy\). Then
\[
|z-1|^2+|z+1|^2=(x-1)^2+y^2+(x+1)^2+y^2=2x^2+2y^2+2.
\]
Setting this equal to \(6\) gives \(2x^2+2y^2+2=6\), so \(x^2+y^2=2\). Hence the locus is a circle centered at the origin with radius \(\sqrt{2}\).
questions.hint: Write \(z=x+iy\), expand the squared moduli, and simplify.

questions.question: The locus of points \(z\) satisfying \(\arg\left(\frac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}\) is

options.label: A
options.text: the upper semicircle of the unit circle centered at the origin, excluding the real-axis endpoints.

options.label: B
options.text: the lower semicircle of the unit circle centered at the origin, excluding the real-axis endpoints.

questions.explanation:
Let \(z=x+iy\). For \(z\ne -1\),
\[
\frac{z-1}{z+1}=\frac{(x-1)+iy}{(x+1)+iy}.
\]
Multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator gives
\[
\frac{z-1}{z+1}=\frac{x^2+y^2-1+2iy}{(x+1)^2+y^2}.
\]
The argument is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) exactly when the real part is \(0\) and the imaginary part is positive. Thus \(x^2+y^2=1\) and \(y>0\). Therefore the locus is the upper semicircle of the unit circle, excluding the real-axis endpoints.
questions.hint: Compute the real and imaginary parts of \(\frac{z-1}{z+1}\), then require the real part to be zero and the imaginary part to be positive.
